source.title: When Representations Align: Universality in Representation Learning Dynamics
source.authors: Loek van Rossem; Andrew M. Saxe

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies whether a proposed theory captures representation-learning dynamics across architectures. It does not measure alignment between representations from independently trained models, scaling of such alignment, or any other listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports within-model representational distances and structures, including their dependence on initialization and task. These are related findings, but they do not measure cross-model representational convergence; the rows below are therefore linked to none of the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper fits an effective theory of two-point representation dynamics to individual networks of many architectures. It never measures alignment between the representations of different models or seeds. Its 'universality' means a shared fit to the theory, up to fitted effective learning rates, not measured cross-model representational similarity.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also argue that some essentials of representation learning may come from gradient descent itself rather than solely from architectural inductive biases. They stress initial weight scale as crucial for the final structure, and note the theory does not scale to larger datasets and ignores architectural inductive biases.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops and evaluates an effective theory; it does not reproduce either original source's method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that initial weight scale changes the representational regime, the selected hidden-layer depth affects theory fit, and the theory fits Adam training dynamics poorly even though some final-structure predictions remain qualitatively similar.

fits_no_version.finding: Networks with different connectivity and nonlinearities each match the same effective theory of two-point dynamics after fitting two constants (Fig. 2). This is universality of the dynamics, not measured representational alignment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation-learning dynamics are shared across sufficiently expressive architectures, up to rescaled effective learning rates.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix A.6 derives that, as initial weights shrink, the distribution of the final representational distance converges and randomness is removed. At large weights the final structure depends on the random initialization (lazy regime).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Convergence of representations across seeds may hold only in the rich, small-initialization regime. This is a theoretical argument, not a measurement.

fits_no_version.finding: On XOR, same-target pairs merge as the theory predicts in the 20-layer network, but the 2-layer network merges only one pair. On MNIST, distances averaged over 50 seeds correlate 0.703 with the theory (0.512 without the diagonal blocks).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How well within-model representational structure fits the theory depends on architecture, expressivity and initialization scale.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235, 2024
record.problems: The effective theory assumes high expressivity and fits effective learning rates to trajectories. The paper says it has no clear path to larger datasets, does not account for architectural inductive biases, and fits Adam dynamics poorly. Its experiments do not directly test cross-model representational convergence.
record.rows_left_out: No results directly measuring a listed claim version were reported. Other within-model dynamics and toy-task results were not included as separate rows because they do not compare representations across models.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep and no cross-model alignment metric.
No empirical comparison of representations across seeds. Appendix A.6 only argues theoretically that final structure loses its random-init dependence at small weights.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation tests between models.
No cross-model feature or circuit comparison.
No comparison of similarity measures or input distributions for cross-model alignment.
No measurement of how complete cross-model alignment is, or of its causes.

record.verdict_notes: The title's 'representations align' refers to shared dynamics across architectures, not to measured cross-model similarity. No row bears on any version. All three rows are within-model comparisons with theory, so their versions stay ['none'] and cannot_determine is appropriate.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep and no cross-model alignment measurement.
No comparison of representations across random seeds or shared-subspace analysis.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired alignment test between models.
No cross-model interpretable feature or circuit comparison.
No comparison of cross-model convergence across similarity measures, settings, or input distributions.
No test of whether cross-model alignment is incomplete, plateaus, or results from shared data or objectives.

rows.subject: 20-layer fully connected network, 500 units per layer, leaky ReLU
rows.operation_detail: Measured final pairwise hidden-representation distances on the XOR task
rows.measure: Final hidden-representation pairwise distances; same-target-output pairs were predicted to merge
rows.value: The learned representation matches the theory prediction; same-target-output pairs merge at small initial weights.
rows.note: Within-model geometry, not a comparison of representations across models.

rows.subject: 2-layer network
rows.operation_detail: Measured final hidden-representation pairwise distances on the XOR task
rows.measure: Merging of same-target-output pairs in the learned representation
rows.baseline: Theory predicts merging for pairs with the same target output.
rows.value: The theory fails to anticipate the merging of only one pair.
rows.note: This is an architecture-specific result about geometry within a model, not inter-model alignment.

rows.subject: 4-layer fully connected leaky-ReLU network
rows.operation_detail: Compared pairwise representation distances on MNIST with theory predictions
rows.measure: Pearson correlation between pairwise final representation distances and theory predictions
rows.value: 0.703; 0.512 when diagonal blocks are not factored in
rows.note: These correlations compare one model's geometry with a theoretical prediction, not representations across models.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
